name: Seated Machine Lateral Raise
grip: Light neutral grip on machine handles with elbows against roller pads.
description: Abduct both arms outward and upward against padded machine levers while seated, isolating the lateral deltoids through guided resistance.
setup: Adjust the seat height so your shoulder joints align directly with the machine's pivot axes.
Sit tall with your chest or back firmly supported by the torso pad and feet flat on the floor.
Place your upper arms/elbows against the inside of the roller pads, holding the guide handles lightly with elbows bent ~90 degrees.
instructions: Raise both arms outward and upward by driving your elbows into the roller pads until upper arms are parallel to the floor (shoulder height).
Keep your torso completely stationary against the pad, avoiding leaning backward or using body momentum.
Pause briefly at shoulder height, squeezing the lateral deltoids.
Lower the arms slowly under control back to the starting position beside your hips without letting the weight stack crash.
cues: Keep torso glued to the support pad.
commonMistakes: Setting seat too high or too low, misaligning shoulder pivot with machine axis.
Shrugging upper traps to heave the weight up instead of abducting with deltoids.
Swinging the torso backward to generate momentum.

logging.note: Cam shapes, lever lengths, and pulley configurations differ widely across machine brands; record selected stack setting without assuming free-weight equivalency.
